questions.question: Imperialism is best defined as
choices: the exchange of goods between equal trading partners only
a policy or practice of extending a state's influence or control over other peoples or territories
the movement from rural areas to cities
a system of local self-government

questions.question: Which factor helped European imperialism expand during the nineteenth century?
choices: European states had no access to ships
Industrial production reduced demand for resources
Industrial economies sought raw materials, markets, and strategic advantages
Imperial powers rejected overseas investment

questions.question: What happened at the Berlin Conference of 1884–1885?
choices: African leaders formed a single continental government
The United Nations established its charter
The trans-Saharan trade ended
European powers negotiated rules for claiming African territories without African representation

questions.question: Which African state successfully resisted Italian invasion at the Battle of Adwa in 1896?
choices: Ethiopia
Mali
Congo Free State
Algeria

questions.question: What was one cause of the Opium Wars between Britain and Qing China?
choices: A dispute about the Panama Canal
Conflict over trade and Britain's opium commerce in China
A struggle over the American Revolution
A conflict between the Inca and Mexica

questions.question: Which policy did Britain follow in India after the 1857 uprising?
choices: India became an independent republic immediately
The Mughal Empire regained control of all India
The British Crown assumed direct rule from the East India Company
Britain ended its presence in South Asia

questions.question: How did imperial powers often justify expansion during the nineteenth century?
choices: They always described expansion as a partnership of equals
They rejected racial ideologies
They stated that resources were irrelevant
They used claims about civilization, religion, or progress to rationalize control

questions.question: Which outcome was common in colonized regions under imperial rule?
choices: Local economies were often reorganized to serve imperial needs
All local political structures remained unchanged
Industrial wealth was distributed equally
Colonial rule eliminated coercion

questions.question: Why did imperial powers value strategic ports and canals?
choices: They prevented ships from carrying goods
They could support military movement and protect trade routes
They eliminated the need for navies
They had no connection to overseas empire

questions.question: The Meiji government in Japan pursued rapid modernization partly in response to
choices: the collapse of the Inca Empire
the end of the Silk Road in antiquity
the threat of Western imperial pressure
the discovery of the Nile

questions.question: What was one effect of imperial borders drawn without regard to local communities?
choices: They always matched existing cultural boundaries
They removed all political conflict
They prevented later debates about sovereignty
They could divide related groups or combine communities with differing interests

questions.question: Why is it inaccurate to describe colonized peoples as passive during imperial expansion?
choices: People resisted, negotiated, adapted, and built political movements in varied ways
Imperial powers acted without any local response
Colonized societies had no leaders or institutions
Resistance never affected imperial policy

questions.question: Which event is associated with the beginning of the Scramble for Africa?
choices: The formation of the Mali Empire
The rapid partition of African territories among European powers in the late nineteenth century
The opening of the Suez Canal in ancient Egypt
The end of the transatlantic slave trade in the fifteenth century

questions.question: A colonial government builds railways mainly to move minerals from interior regions to ports. What does this suggest about infrastructure under imperialism?
choices: It always connected every community equally
It was unrelated to economic goals
It often served extraction and export as well as local transportation
It eliminated colonial control

questions.question: Which statement best describes economic imperialism?
choices: A country's citizens vote in local elections
A trade exchange with equal bargaining power
A policy of avoiding all foreign investment
A powerful state or company gains influence over another economy without necessarily annexing its territory

questions.question: Why did nationalist movements grow in many colonized regions?
choices: People sought greater political control and challenged foreign rule
Imperial rule always granted immediate independence
Nationalism opposed every local culture
Colonial borders prevented political organization

questions.question: What was one consequence of imperial competition among European powers?
choices: It ended all conflicts in Europe
It increased international rivalries and contributed to tensions before World War I
It created a single European government
It removed competition for resources

questions.question: A historian compares colonial tax records with oral histories from residents. What can this reveal?
choices: The exact opinions of every resident
That taxation affected no local economy
How official policies affected people whose experiences may be absent from government records
That oral histories cannot be evidence

questions.question: Which term describes a territory controlled politically or economically by an outside power?
choices: City-state
Federation
Common market
Colony

questions.question: Why can imperialism's long-term effects differ across regions?
choices: Local histories, forms of resistance, colonial policies, and postcolonial choices varied
Every empire used identical policies everywhere
Geography has no effect on historical outcomes
Independence produced identical economies in all countries
